solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Carry on Australian bird series which was put back

indicators.note: put back tells us the two pieces before it are written in the reverse direction

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: Someone continuing after a run of Australian bird sightings was postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' sounds like postponement but tells you to read the bird and series pieces backwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on after a pause is to take up again, the verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Puts in new pipes with bumpers left off

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad or wrong signals that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mechanic replaces a car's piping after the bumpers have been taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like the bumpers being removed, but it is the anagram signal on BUMPERS plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumber fits pipes; doing that again in a building is a re-fitting of its plumbing.

clue.text: Playwright's shop close to collapse

indicators.note: a building set to collapse falls into pieces, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A dramatist's shop is about to fall down.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'Playwright's' stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek tragedian who wrote Oedipus Rex is one of the most famous dramatists of antiquity.

clue.text: Initially, Ricky Gervais featured in the most important side

indicators.note: featured in says the initials appear inside the following piece

parts.note: main means most important, as in the main event

indicators.note: Initially picks out the first letters of the two words of the name

explanation.surface: The comedian Ricky Gervais appeared in the most important show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' as a definition is a stretch: the edge or border of a page or area.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is the edge or border of something, like the side of a page.

clue.text: Attacks pies, does badly

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of the two words are done in a disordered way

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into pies and makes a poor job of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attacks' looks like eating greedily but means bouts of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Bouts or fits of an illness, such as attacks of asthma, are called episodes.

clue.text: Player gets lively chap to fry eggs

indicators.note: lively suggests energetic movement, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sportsman gets an energetic fellow to cook him some eggs for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' means an actor here: Dame Peggy Ashcroft was a leading English stage and film actress.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is an actor, and this dame was a celebrated twentieth-century Shakespearean actress.

clue.text: Playwright born a Native American

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw was the Irish dramatist
née, French for born, introduces a woman's maiden name

explanation.surface: A dramatist who was born an indigenous American.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shawnee are an indigenous people of North America, originally of the Ohio Valley.

clue.text: Medical man setter has shot in play

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
the setter refers to himself as I, so the setter has is I've

explanation.surface: A doctor who writes crosswords has taken a photograph during a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: IVE is the contraction I've with the apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf or cricket a powerful forward stroke of the ball is called by this name.

clue.text: Extremely reasonable hospital is in Versailles

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital
in French, as spoken at Versailles, is translates as est

explanation.surface: A very sensible hospital is located in the French palace town.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of sensible or rational: the most level-headed of all.

clue.text: Half a pill for every player

indicators.note: Half a asks for the front half of the word pill

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: Each performer gets half a tablet.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who plays the bagpipes or pipe is a player of an instrument.

clue.text: Diminutive cat not unknown around a play

indicators.note: around says the following piece is put inside the pieces before it
not tells us to leave out the unknown letter

parts.note: pygmy means very small
Y is a mathematical unknown
a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A tiny cat, quite well known, prowls around.
explanation.walkthrough: PYGMY loses Y (an algebraic unknown) to give PYGM; with LION it surrounds A.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw's comedy about a flower girl, later adapted as the musical My Fair Lady.

clue.text: Blood flowing here ruins play — mourn 40% of investment

indicators.note: ruins as a verb means wrecks, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt
40% of a ten-letter word is its first four letters

explanation.surface: A wrecked theatre production leaves investors grieving for their lost money.
explanation.walkthrough: '40% of' takes INVE from investment; with PLAY and MOURN the anagram is signalled by 'ruins'.
explanation.definitionFit: This vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart, so blood flows through it.

clue.text: Like wife buxom, naked, and ready for some Arabs

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer layer, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: ready is slang for cash, and the rial is the currency of Oman and Yemen

explanation.surface: A curvaceous wife, undressed and prepared for some Arab men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' means money, as in ready cash.
explanation.definitionFit: From Latin uxor, wife: the adjective describes something pertaining to a married woman.

clue.text: Campaign for vote against return for baseball players

indicators.note: return means come back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to seek something is to campaign or strive for it
a nay is a no vote

explanation.surface: A political campaign in which the vote went against a candidate's return.
explanation.walkthrough: SEEK + NAY read backwards gives the team name.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York team of Major League Baseball, its players collectively known by this nickname.

clue.text: Labour reverse course with Liberal and co-operate to play this

indicators.note: to reverse course is to turn back, so the party abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: LAB is the abbreviation for the Labour Party

explanation.surface: Labour does a U-turn and works with the Liberals in a coalition.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'play ball' is an idiom for co-operating.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom play ball means to co-operate, so this is what one plays when co-operating.

clue.text: Most of 10 across arranged for group singing "Yakety-Yak"

indicators.note: arranged signals putting the letters into a new order
Most of drops the last letter of the number word

parts.note: the number ten

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to another clue, rearranged for a vocal group's hit.
explanation.walkthrough: '10 across' looks like a cross-reference but is literally TEN and ACROSS; TE plus ACROSS is rearranged. The Coasters were a 1950s American vocal group.
explanation.definitionFit: The American doo-wop group had their best-known hit with this 1958 song about household chores.

clue.text: Stone doing his usual thing walking along

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds
a rolling stone, as in the proverb or the band, is one that is rolling

explanation.surface: A Rolling Stone carries on as normal, ambling along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his usual thing' points to the Rolling Stones band and the proverb 'a rolling stone gathers no moss'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroll is to walk at a leisurely pace, so this describes someone ambling along.

clue.text: Play this poem about fruit contrariwise

indicators.note: about would normally put the poem around the fruit
contrariwise flips that, so the fruit goes around the poem

parts.note: a melon is a fruit
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A performer is told to act out a poem about fruit, the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrariwise' flips 'about', so the fruit wraps the poem rather than the poem wrapping the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A small accordion-like reed instrument that a musician plays.

clue.text: Condiment South African butcher's missing, oddly after bishop leaves apology

indicators.note: after places the South African and butcher pieces following the apology piece
leaves means departs from, so the letters for the bishop are taken out

parts.note: sorry is an apology
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
SA is the abbreviation for South Africa

indicators.note: missing says certain letters are removed
oddly says the odd-numbered letters are the ones missing

parts.note: the 's stands for is, joining the butcher to missing

explanation.surface: A South African butcher strangely lacks a condiment after the bishop leaves an apology.
explanation.walkthrough: RR (Right Reverend) leaves SORRY to give SOY; even letters of BUTCHER give UCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A salty dark sauce made from fermented soya beans, used as a seasoning in Asian cooking.

clue.text: We get upset finding a eulogy oddly missing

indicators.note: get upset means to be knocked over, signalling a rearrangement
oddly missing removes the odd-numbered letters, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: We are distressed to find a funeral speech that is somehow missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Even letters of 'finding a eulogy' give IDNAUOY, which 'get upset' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The first-person plural pronoun covers the speaker plus one other person addressed: the pair together.

clue.text: Maybe pine for Beerbohm?

definitions.meaning: a pine is an example of a conifer of the woods
Sir Herbert Beerbohm ... was a Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: Someone longs for the writer Max Beerbohm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like a verb (to long for); it is the conifer. Beerbohm here is the actor-manager Herbert Beerbohm Tree, Max's half-brother.
explanation.definitionFit: A pine is an example of a woody plant, and the actor's surname is the same word.

clue.text: Every hundred years, 20 successfully play

parts.note: a score is twenty
read as a period of one hundred years, with A meaning each or per, as in once a week

explanation.surface: Every hundred years, twenty people perform well.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman's hundred runs is a century, the high point of an innings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer makes a hundred runs in one innings: a notable success at the crease.

clue.text: Browser starts to chew hawthorns to the north of city

indicators.note: in a down clue, to the north of means placed above, so before
starts to picks out the opening letters of the two words that follow

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital city

explanation.surface: A grazing animal begins chewing hawthorns north of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browser' looks like a grazing animal but is Google's web browser.
explanation.definitionFit: Google's web browser is software for viewing websites, a computer browser.

clue.text: See 20
New area for mollusc production

parts.note: an acre is a unit of area

explanation.surface: A new site set aside for shellfish farming.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother-of-pearl is the iridescent substance produced by molluscs to line their shells.

clue.text: Play game

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's tragedy of the Moor of Venice
a board game of black and white counters, also called reversi

explanation.definitionFit: The title names both Shakespeare's tragedy and a board game played with two-coloured discs.

clue.text: With difficulty, cover rent and do another makeover

indicators.note: With difficulty suggests the letters are struggled into a new order

explanation.surface: Struggling to pay the rent, someone renovates the place once again.
explanation.definitionFit: To convert something again, transforming it a second time, is a repeated makeover.

clue.text: Pointed arch with no play

parts.note: O is zero or nothing, so it stands for no
play means slack or give, as in a loose rope

explanation.surface: A pointed arch built with no flexibility at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' means slack or looseness here, not a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: In Gothic architecture this is the term for a pointed arch or diagonal rib of a vault.

clue.text: Pain 19 treated with mild laxative

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to clue 19, the actor-manager's surname, also a pine

explanation.surface: Pain in the actor-manager is treated with a gentle remedy for constipation.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' stands for the answer to 19, TREE, anagrammed with PAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle purgative that opens the bowels, from Latin aperire, to open.

clue.text: Old football player, say, grabbed by a much older player

indicators.note: grabbed by says the example piece is held inside the actor piece

parts.note: Edmund Kean was a celebrated English actor of the early 1800s
say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A veteran footballer is seized by an even older sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' means an actor in the wordplay: Edmund Kean. Kevin Keegan was an England footballer of the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Kevin Keegan was an England and Liverpool forward, later a manager, now a retired footballer.
